thread:
Nikhil: noticed a big spike in dashboard LCP + lots of chunk revalidate network requests from clients after the infra tweak. map tiles and sparklines hang for ~1-2s each. Anybody else seeing this? :thinking:
Sofia: yep, repeated 304/200s for app.<locale>.js and a bunch of /tile endpoints showing 503s then 200s. started ~09:03 after the rollout.
Ravi: linked to the routing policy change that enabled region_fallback for EU->US to avoid capacity gaps? That can cause requests to flip host pools and bust our chunk/cdn affinity.
Kara: deploy log: ops-bot deployed routing-policy v2.4 (region_fallback enabled) at 09:01 UTC. ops-bot: deploy 6790012200 (routing-policy-v2.4) completed by Liz at 09:01:08 UTC
Liz: telemetry shows client-side chunk revalidation: lots of If-Modified-Since headers hitting CDN origin instead of edge cache (miss due to new host mapping). Example from logs:
```
[09:04:12] WARN cdn: origin-revalidate path=/static/js/app.en-US.js status=200 cache_status=MISS host=eu-node-3
[09:04:12] INFO frontend: tile-fetch path=/tiles/heat/23/45/12 user=ui-test took=1123ms host=us-node-2
[09:04:13] WARN route: pool-switch route=/api/tiles code=503 fallback_pool=us_pool
```
Sofia: interesting edge case: our chunk URL signing uses region as part of the cache key (to enforce geo-based TTL). region_fallback switches region hint and client gets a different signed URL -> cache miss.
Nikhil: two things: (1) for immediate mitigation, can we disable region_fallback or temporarily pin dashboard traffic to the original pool? (2) longer-term we need signed URL scheme decoupled from runtime route pool and prefer a CDN-level routing header instead.
Ravi: mitigation options: disable feature (fast), or add sticky-affinity by client-cookie so chunk URLs stay consistent per session (needs small change to auth service), or bump edge TTL to reduce revalidates (risky for real rollouts).
Kara: ops-bot can rollback routing-policy v2.4. I can flip it now. Also suggest we run a small canary with affinity-preserving header: `X-Affinity: prefer=eu_pool` so clients keep edge key consistent.
Liz: I'll watch Sentry and RUM. If we rollback, we should also surface a UX banner on dashboard for 10 minutes explaining degraded tile load to reduce support noise.
Sofia: for postmortem: add a unit test that ensures signed asset URL transformation is invariant to pool mapping. This would have caught region->pool coupling.
Ravi: agree. I'll file a follow-up: link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2345 (prefetch/asset-signing decoupling).
ops-bot: rolling back deploy 6790012200 -> intent=rollback_by_Kara initiated at 09:07:01 UTC
Kara: rollback done 09:08:45 UTC. RUM numbers trending back to baseline but leaving extra TTL on edge for 20m to let the CDN warm.
Nikhil: thanks. action items: Ravi -> write invariant test + RFC for decoupling; Sofia -> patch auth to support cookie-affinity quick toggle; Liz -> draft short support note; Kara -> run a controlled canary with X-Affinity header once RFC is approved. ETA: sync in 2 hours. :thumbsup:
